practicals.label: Activity 7.1
practicals.bookText:
The following compounds are provided in the form of liquid or in the
form of their aqueous solutions. Use blue and red litmus paper strips to show
whether these substances are acidic or basic in their aqueous solutions.
| Substance | Acidic | Basic |
|---|---|---|
| Tap water | | |
| Battery water | | |
| Rain water | | |
| Soap solution | | |
| Tooth paste | | |
| Shampoo | | |
| Bleach | | |
EXERCISE (in-text)
In what ways are mineral acids useful for us?
procedure: Take small samples of the provided substances in separate, labelled containers.
Test each sample with a clean blue litmus paper strip and a clean red litmus paper strip.
Observe and record any colour change for each strip, then identify the substance as acidic or basic.
practicals.aim: To use blue and red litmus paper strips to determine whether the provided substances are acidic or basic in aqueous solution.

viva.question: What happens to blue litmus in an acidic solution?
What happens to red litmus in a basic solution?
What do you conclude if neither litmus strip changes colour?
viva.answer: The sample is neutral, or its acidity or basicity is too weak to show a change with litmus.

viva.question: Why should a fresh strip be used for each sample?
viva.answer: To prevent one sample from contaminating another.

viva.question: What may happen when red litmus is placed in bleach?
viva.answer: It may turn blue at first and then lose its colour as the bleach acts on the dye.

apparatus: Provided liquid samples or aqueous solutions

rows: Usually remains blue at first; may fade
May turn blue briefly, then fade or bleach

practicals.title: Testing substances with litmus paper
precautions: Use a clean dropper and separate labelled containers for the samples.
Use a fresh strip for each test and avoid touching the test area with fingers.
Do not taste or directly smell any sample.
Avoid contact with battery water and bleach; rinse any splashes on skin immediately with plenty of water.
Do not mix the samples with one another.
practicals.result: Battery water, rain water and shampoo showed acidic behaviour, while soap solution, toothpaste and bleach showed basic behaviour. Tap water showed no change with either litmus strip.

practicals.label: Activity 7.2
practicals.bookText:
Take a few granules of zinc in a clean test tube. Add dilute H₂SO₄ in it and heat it gently. Identify the gas evolved in this reaction by taking a burning match stick near the mouth of test tube. Note the observations in your notebook.
3. They decompose metal carbonates and hydrogen carbonates evolving carbon dioxide gas.
CaCO₃ (s) + 2HCl (aq) → CaCl₂ (aq) + H₂O (l) + CO₂ (g)
2NaHCO₃ (s) + H₂SO₄ (aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l) + 2CO₂ (g)
procedure: Take a few granules of zinc in a clean test tube.
Take a burning match stick near the mouth of the test tube to identify the gas evolved.
Note the observations in your notebook.
practicals.aim: To identify the gas evolved when zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid.

viva.question: Which gas is evolved when zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid?
What observation identifies hydrogen gas?
viva.answer: It burns with a characteristic ‘pop’ sound when tested with a burning match stick.

viva.question: What type of reaction occurs between zinc and dilute sulfuric acid?
What salt is formed in this reaction?
Why should the test tube be heated gently?
viva.answer: To avoid rapid reaction and splashing of the acid.

rows: Effervescence; gas burns with a ‘pop’ sound
Bubbles form; gas burns with a ‘pop’ sound

practicals.diagram: Draw a test tube containing zinc granules and dilute H₂SO₄, held with a test-tube holder and heated gently by a burner; show a burning match stick near the mouth of the test tube and label the zinc granules, dilute H₂SO₄, test tube, test-tube holder, burner, hydrogen gas, and burning match stick.
practicals.title: Identification of hydrogen from zinc and dilute sulfuric acid
precautions: Use only a few zinc granules and dilute sulfuric acid.
Hold the test tube with a holder and keep its mouth pointed away from yourself and others.
Keep the burning match stick near the mouth of the test tube, not inside it.
Wear safety goggles and avoid contact with the acid.
practicals.result: Zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid to evolve hydrogen gas, which burns with a ‘pop’ sound.

practicals.label: Activity 7.3
practicals.bookText:
How to clean a blocked drain?
Blocked drains are one of the most common problems that we face every other day. Different blockages require different chemicals to remove them.
One of the ways to clean the drain is to pour half a cup of sodium bicarbonate solution into the drain followed by half a cup of vinegar. Cover the drain and wait for thirty minutes. Pour boiling water down the drain.
Caustic chemical drain cleaners are capable of dissolving grease, hair, food and other common blockages. Pour down the caustic cleaner into your drain. Wait for half an hour and then flush your drain with water.
procedure: For the bicarbonate-and-vinegar method, pour half a cup of sodium bicarbonate solution into the blocked drain, followed by half a cup of vinegar.
Cover the drain and wait for thirty minutes.
Pour boiling water down the drain.
Alternatively, pour caustic chemical drain cleaner down the drain, following its label and using it only with adult supervision.
Wait for half an hour and then flush the drain with water.
Do not use the caustic cleaner together with vinegar or any other cleaner.
practicals.aim: To describe how different chemicals can be used to help clear a blocked drain.

viva.question: What gas is produced when sodium bicarbonate reacts with vinegar?
What is vinegar’s main acidic component?
What kind of substance is sodium bicarbonate?
Why should a caustic drain cleaner be handled carefully?
viva.answer: It is corrosive and can cause severe burns.

viva.question: Why should different drain cleaners not be mixed?
viva.answer: They may react dangerously and produce heat or harmful substances.

practicals.title: Cleaning a blocked drain
precautions: Wear protective gloves and eye protection when handling drain cleaners.
Use caustic drain cleaner only with adult supervision and follow its label.
Never mix caustic drain cleaner with vinegar or any other cleaner.
Keep boiling water and chemicals away from skin and eyes; pour carefully.
Keep the area well ventilated and keep children away from the drain.
practicals.result: Sodium bicarbonate solution and vinegar react to produce carbon dioxide, which may help loosen a blockage. Caustic drain cleaner may dissolve some common blockage materials, but it must be handled with great care.
